items.text: That does not mean nobody should trade for a living.
Experience alone does not fix the odds.

blocks.heading: Trading Financial Markets Full-Time Is a Real

items.text: "Good career" here does not mean "everyone who tries this can win" or "with enough discipline, the odds reverse for you personally." It also does not mean "avoid it entirely, nobody succeeds."

It means a small number of people build a genuinely strong, scalable career around markets, either as a skilled independent trader with a tested edge and real risk control, or inside a regulated firm where someone else's capital is on the line.

blocks.heading: Almost No "How to Start Trading" Content

items.text: What "full-time trading" actually costs to attempt safely
Beyond trading capital itself, you need 6-12 months of full living expenses set aside separately, since income in the early period is unpredictable and can be negative for a stretch.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: A friend's story about a "trader who quit his job and never looked back," or a screenshot of one good month, will not tell you whether this actually fits your money, your temperament, and your real situation.
Trading rewards people who can sit with genuine uncertainty for hours, follow a rule even when it feels wrong in the moment, and treat a loss as data instead of a personal failure.
If the appeal is mainly the idea of fast money or "being your own boss," test that specific pull directly with a small, real position before betting a career on it.

blocks.heading: Three Proofs Before You Go Full-Time

items.text: The four questions tells you whether trading fits on paper.
Do not go full-time before passing all three proofs, with a documented, verifiable track record.

Trade a real, small live account (not a demo, not a backtest) for a stretch long enough to include a genuine losing streak, and come out with a documented, rule-based process, not a story about one good week.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That End Trading Careers Early

items.text: Trading full-time from day one adds financial pressure to every single trade, which is exactly the condition most likely to produce the panicked, oversized bets that blow up an account.
SEBI has repeatedly warned about, and taken action against, unregistered "finfluencers" and paid tip or signal groups.

blocks.heading: Safer Adjacent Careers in and Around Markets

items.text: If the pull toward trading is really a pull toward markets, data, and decision-making under uncertainty, several salaried paths let you build that same interest with a firm's capital at risk instead of your own, and with a defined ceiling that can go quite high at senior levels.
Quantitative or algorithmic trading roles

Hired into proprietary trading firms, hedge funds, or bank trading desks, usually through strong mathematics, statistics, computer science, or engineering skills, salaried with performance-linked pay, firm capital at risk, not yours.

visuals.heading: Every Rupee of Risk Is Yours

blocks.heading: Retail Self-Directed Trading: You Open a Demat

items.text: Professional or institutional trading: you are hired, often after a quantitative or finance-heavy hiring process, into a role at a proprietary trading firm, hedge fund, brokerage, or bank.
Both are legitimate.
You risk your own savings on every trade.
SEBI's own data says roughly 9 out of 10 people who try this lose money, and losses often widen with more experience, not less.
No PF, no gratuity, no employer health cover, no paid leave.
The ceiling is real for a tiny minority, some traders do compound capital into serious wealth, but it is not the median outcome, it is the exception SEBI's data explicitly measures.
Is the person or platform actually SEBI-registered as an Investment Adviser or Research Analyst.
Are they showing a verified, audited track record, or curated screenshots of good trades.
If their method genuinely worked reliably, why are they selling it to strangers instead of trading it themselves.
Does the pitch promise a guaranteed return, "sure-shot" calls, or fast, effortless income.

blocks.heading: What to Tell a Worried Family

items.text: Fear that "trading" means gambling away savings with nothing to show for it.
Stories about people who lost a lot of money fast, or who quietly stopped talking about their trading account.
Not knowing whether this is a real plan or a way to avoid a harder job search or a difficult decision.
